title: Reduction of the proper bound to a lattice on a stratum
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$, a field $k$ of positive characteristic different from $\ell$, an algebraic closure $\Qlb$ of $\mathbf Q_\ell$, and a finite subextension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ of $\Qlb$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Let $X,Y$ be separated schemes of finite type over $k$, as in [sk-def-sfb-dc-setting], let $p\colon X\to Y$ be a proper $k$-morphism [def-weil-proper-morphism], and let $c\in\mathbf Z$. Put $\Lambda=E$ or $\Qlb$. For finite subextensions $F/\mathbf Q_\ell$ of $\Qlb$ and their rings of integers use their condensed topological rings [sk-def-sfb-condensed-ring]; for $\Qlb$ use the finite-subextension-valued condensed ring of [sk-def-sfb-qlbar-condensed]. For each coefficient ring $A$ below, $A_T$ denotes its pulled-back condensed ring on the small pro-étale site [sk-def-sfb-pulled-back-coefficients], and modules are module objects [sk-def-sfb-module-objects]. Write $R^qp_*$ for the right derived functors of the additive left exact module pushforward [def-sfb-module-lower-star], with $R^qp_*=0$ for $q<0$.

For a locally closed immersion $a\colon S\hookrightarrow X$ [def-weil-closed-immersion], write $a_!=i_*u_!$, where $u\colon S\hookrightarrow\overline S$ is open and $i\colon\overline S\hookrightarrow X$ is closed, as in [sk-lem-coefficient-heart]. Lisse finite free means locally free of finite rank for the pro-étale topology, with ranks allowed to vary. For an $\mathcal O_{F,T}$-module $N$, set $N[1/\ell]=F_T\otimes_{\mathcal O_{F,T}}N$, and for an $F_T$-module $P$ put $P_{\Qlb}=\Qlb_T\otimes_{F_T}P$; these are ordinary extension-of-scalars functors [sk-def-sfb-change-of-scalars] along the coefficient maps [sk-def-sfb-coefficient-change].

Suppose that for every locally closed immersion $a\colon S\hookrightarrow X$, every finite extension $F/E$ inside $\Qlb$ (including $F=E$), and every lisse finite free $\mathcal O_{F,S}$-module $L_0$, one has
$$R^qp_*(a_!L_0)=0\qquad(q>c),$$
and that this vanishing also holds for $(a_!L_0)[1/\ell]$ and for $((a_!L_0)[1/\ell])_{\Qlb}$. Then
$$R^qp_*M=0\qquad(q>c)$$
for every $M\in\Cons(X,\Lambda)$ [sk-def-sfb-constructible].

proof.text: Let P assert vanishing of R^q p_* for every nonnegative q greater than c simultaneously. The actual module categories have enough injectives. The full right-derived long exact sequence makes P closed under extensions; additivity makes it contain zero and be invariant under isomorphisms. For a finite chain of subobjects, use the short exact sequences of successive cokernels and Fin.induction to propagate P from the successive quotients to the whole object. This also handles q=0 and negative c.

Finite type over the field makes X Noetherian. Clause (11) of coefficientHeart supplies a finite subobject filtration of any constructible module with quotients isomorphic to locally closed extensions of lisse modules. The preceding induction reduces the assertion to each such lisse extension. Locally closed subschemes of X are Noetherian, so the coefficient descent theorem applies to them.

For a lisse finite-field coefficient module on S, use the existing lattice-subquotient filtration of its locally closed extension to X. Its successive quotients are ordinary rationalizations of extensions of integral lisse lattices along composite immersions into X. Transport the filtration from the universe-lifted spectral-norm coefficients to the original finite intermediate field. Use the proved coefficient-isomorphism, comap-extension, and lattice-small helpers in IntegralModelsGenerators, not that module's derived-generation conclusion. Local freeness in the raw coefficient presentation is equivalent to IsLisseCoefficientModule. The premise for F=E gives P on each quotient, hence on the lisse extension.

For an algebraic-closure lisse module, descend it to a finite field F0 using coefficient_finite_descent_lisse. Choose a finite common upper bound F of E and F0 in the directed poset of finite subfields; its directedness is proved by the finite compositum construction, so E is contained in F. Ordinary scalar extension of the descended module to F stays locally free, and the existing extendScalarsComp and coefficient-map composition isomorphisms identify its algebraic-closure extension with the original module. These are ordinary tensor comparisons, so no comparison with a derived scalar functor is needed.

Apply the finite-field lattice argument to the inverse image of P under ordinary scalar extension F to Qbar. This property is closed under extensions because that scalar extension is exact. The third clause of the premise gives it on every rationalized integral stratum lattice, with the required E <= F. The proved ordinary extension-scalar comparison for open followed by closed extension identifies the resulting object with the original lisse extension. Apply the outer constructible filtration induction. All integer c are covered because the proof works separately for every natural q with c < q.

split_report.summary: Retained the previous statement and lattice route; checked every cited current statement. Separated the long scalar, geometric, and filtration arguments into seven steps and reused existing subfield and algebraic-closure flatness lemmas instead of hiding those comparisons inline. Generated current verbatim witnesses for every citation. No new nodes and no statement change.
split_report.blueprint: Step 1 realizes Extensions; Steps 2 and 4 realize Strata and its ambient hypotheses; Steps 3 and 5–7 realize Lattices, including exact scalar change, global refinement, extension-by-zero comparison, and the final filtration induction.

tool_uses.why: The general ringed-site theorem supplies Grothendieck module categories on the actual pro-étale coefficient sheaves; this ambient homological input is not a step of the proper-bound unit.
Enough injectives for a Grothendieck category verifies the hypothesis of the long-exact-sequence tool.
The general derived-functor long exact sequence supplies extension stability; no node of this proper-bound unit states this homological fact.
Generic finite-type Noetherianity verifies the hypotheses of the existing stratification and filtration tools.
Generic Noetherian-open quasi-compactness verifies that locally closed strata remain finite type over k.
Generic ordering and refinement of finite strata implements the refinement already required in the proper-bound route.
Generic filtration with specified stratum quotients implements the open–closed dévissage required by the unit.

Generic coefficient-change compatibility with restriction and extension by zero identifies the lattice and target-coefficient pieces; the proper-bound unit has no separate statement of this compatibility.
The generic pulled-back coefficient colimits give localization and the filtered finite-field union used to identify ordinary and derived scalar change.
Cartesian coefficients identify the restricted rings in the localization tool, and finite freeness proves exactness of finite field scalar change.
Generic quasi-separatedness checks the qcqs hypotheses of the arbitrary-ring localization tool.
The generic ring-sheaf theorem proves exactness of open extension and closed direct image also for integral coefficients; the rational coefficient-heart statement alone does not supply that case.
Finite-field scalar extension exactness is a generic coefficient tool needed for the scalar comparison, without replacing the lattice route.
Algebraic-closure scalar extension exactness is the existing generic flatness input explicitly required by the blueprint Lattices paragraph.

The delivery re-splits the already reviewed item into 7 steps: statement and stmt_deps are unchanged, there are no new nodes, and the unit record is untouched. Statement: compared with the main-20261015 .md, it covers every F/E in Qlb including F=E, its 'also holds' is equivalent to the source's 'passes to', and it adds the standing setting explicitly. It is not weakened. It is a lemma, not a target, so there is no base-change morphism to check; the coefficients are module objects over the pulled-back O_F, F and Qlb throughout. Checks by step: S1, the Grothendieck module category from prop-pur-kinjective plus enough injectives make the long exact sequence of lem-weil-pbc-derived-functor-long-exact apply, and R^q=0 for q<0 covers negative c. S2, X is Noetherian, strata are finite type (localization and quotient charts) and separated (S->X is a monomorphism, so the diagonal is a base change of the closed one), and qcqs. S3, F_T=O_F[1/l] from qlbar-colimit-x, tensor = l-colimit (checked through the universal property), lem-sfb-subfield-flat and lem-sfb-qlbar-flat plus the left adjoint give exactness, and LF=D(F) holds because sk-def-sfb-coefficient-change defines the tensor as L(Ext). S4, only clause (1) of the two-colimit theorem is used, and the compositum EF_0 is a field. S5, the stratified lattice is lisse = locally free of finite rank, as the premise needs; the immersion composition is written out, and the ordered refinement comes from common-stratification (1). S6, u_! and i_* are exact for an arbitrary ring sheaf on qcqs schemes, and coherence gives a_!=i_*u_!. S7, the filtration quotients a_k!(M|S_k), transported by scalar-six (2) once or twice, are exactly the sheaves the premise covers. Small cases: X empty, rank 0, a point with c=0 and c=-1, different fields on different strata. Graph: proof_deps equals the union of step uses, every id exists and none is merged, and a DFS finds no cycle. rg over the DAG finds no duplicate; the only related node, det-proper-heart-bound-rational, consumes this item. No SGA.
